newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BUCHWALD SAYS RETURN TO STUTTGART UNLIKELY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BUCHWALD SAYS RETURN TO STUTTGART UNLIKELY.

text.p: Guido Buchwald, a defender in Germany's 1990 World Cup winning team, said on Monday it was unlikely he would return to his former side, Bundesliga leaders VfB Stuttgart.
But three other Bundesliga teams are reportedly interested in signing Buchwald, 35, who is under contract with the Urawa Red Diamonds in Japan's J-league until December 31.

Buchwald, an international until 1994 when he left to play in Japan, told the newspaper Kicker recently he wants to return to Germany in January "at the latest" and Stuttgart was his first choice, although other clubs were interested.

But he told regional television station Suedwestfunk he had tried to call Stuttgart president Gerhard Mayer-Vorfelder 10 days ago. Buchwald said Mayer-Vorfelder's secretary said he would call him back, but he never did.

"Last summer he said he definitely wanted me back," said Buchwald, who helped Stuttgart to their 1992 championship. "But if he thinks I would be a disturbance, then it is better we don't even reopen this chapter."
Local media reports have suggested that Mayer-Vorfelder and Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew were concerned that Buchwald's return could upset the team's balance.
Buchwald reportedly has received other offers from St Pauli, Hansa Rostock and Bochum.
